# Sector Post-Session Review — Industrials (XLI)

**Primary driver: Fresh US hard-data miss on the sector's own spine — the G.17 Industrial Production report released this morning (Aug 18).** US industrial production posted **0% growth in July**, missing expectations of +0.1% to +0.3%, with manufacturing output stagnating for a second straight month. **Secondary drivers (interacting):**
- **Global bond rout / rising yields.** 30-year Treasury yield near two-year highs; global bond selloff deepened. Rising real yields pressure long-duration industrial and AI-power names.
- **Oil above $90/$91 with live Hormuz tension.** Brent surpassed $91; Hormuz attacks slowing tanker movement. While this is a tailwind for oil-linked/energy-equipment names, the broad risk-off effect dominated.
- **AI-power leadership rolling over.** GE Vernova tumbled ~5-6% (continuing post-earnings pullback); Eaton's Q3 EPS estimates were cut by Zacks on Aug 18. The sector's strongest structural sub-theme (AI power/grid) is now a drag, not a cushion.
- **Broad risk-off tape.** Tech-led decline (Nasdaq slide), ES/NQ sharply negative premarket.
